newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakofarma shares a long-term buy - ING.
newsitem.headline: Slovakofarma shares a long-term buy - ING.

text.p: Shares of Slovakofarma a.s., Slovakia's largest drug producer, are a long-term buy, a report by ING Barings said on Thursday.

It said Slovakofarma's acquisition of a 40 percent stake in major penicilin maker Biotika and a deal to supply U.S. optical giant Bausch and Lomb with an eye-drop base should substantially boost the company's bottom line.
"This, combined with the company's democratic attitude to minority shareholders with regard to profit distribution makes the company attractive to long-term institutional investors," the report said.
It put its recommendation at 3,050 crowns, as of August 30. On Tuesday Slovakofarma shares closed at 3,100 crowns on the Bratislava Stock Exchange.
Slovakofarma posted a 481.2 million crown net-profit for 1995, up from 389.6 million crowns in 1994, while overall sales totalled four billion crowns from 3.3 billion crowns the previous year.
ING estimated the firm's 1996 net profit would hit 525 million crowns and 550 million in 1997.
The firm approved a 1995 gross dividend of 250 crowns, after paying a 146 crown dividend in 1994, the highest dividend paid out so far by a leading publicly traded Slovak firm.

A company linked to Slovakofarma management recently took over Biotika, Slovakia's major producer of antibiotics, despite protests by Biotika management and employees who had made their own bid in the company's privatisation project.
